newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profit-taking caps dlr in Tokyo, but stays strong.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking caps dlr in Tokyo, but stays strong.

text.p: 0015 GMT --*Dollar capped versus yen in early Tokyo on Friday due to light profit-taking, but maintained overnight gains due to persistent buying demand by interbank operators.
*Mark also fell slightly against yen on profit-taking after rising sharply above 64.12 yen overnight.

*"Interbank dealers are eager to pick up dollars on dips following unexpected rallies against the yen overnight," said a spot dealer at a Japanese city bank. "But we are a bit cautious about buying aggressively now ahead of the release of Japanese trade data on Monday."
*Underlying dollar sentiment improved rapidly after speculative and technical buying led by U.S. fund operators pushed up dollar versus yen.
*Dealers said there was a wide variety of yen-selling speculation, including worries about the economic recovery in Japan, which pushed down the yen overnight.
*Concern that a Southeast Asian currency crisis may hurt Japan's fragile economy also depressed the yen overnight.
*Yen's slump commenced after Indonesia announced a de facto float of its currency on Thursday, following similar action by neighbouring countries in recent weeks.
*Activity is expected to be thin today as many Tokyo operators are on "Obon" summer holidays.
*"The market is led by interbank operators with many Japanese corporations out today," the dealer said. "Moves in the dollar/yen rate could be exaggerated in thin trade."
*Technical reasons likely to keep dollar capped with 90-day moving average seen around 117.90 yen and 200-day moving average seen around 118.25 yen.
*"It's very difficult to determine sentiment after the rallies overnight, but for the time being, the market will focus on technicals," a trust bank dealer said.
*Mark also capped above 64.00 yen on profit-taking after rising sharply to 64.12 yen on heavy short-covering overnight.
*At 0035 GMT, mark stood at 63.84/91 yen compared with 64.06 yen in New York overnight. It stood at 63.40 yen in late Tokyo on Thursday.
*Japanese exporters may also sell marks above 64.00 yen. In the short term, the mark is expected to trade in a range of 63.80 to 64.30 yen.
*Dollar closed at 117.78/88 yen and 1.8390/00 in New York on Thursday.
